creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Moving a pane into a tab of its own takes three commands and spawns a shell nobody wanted. Asked for while pulling one busy agent out of a four-way split: *"spawn a new tab with just a specific pane rather than needing this dance"*.

The dance, run on 0.4.1:

    muster tab new --pane p208qd8wn9 --json    # -> p208r93k5w, a new tab with a new pane
    muster pane move --pane p208qd8wn9 --onto p208r93k5w
    muster pane close --pane p208r93k5w        # drop the pane the first command made

It works. What it costs:

- **A real login shell on the far machine**, started and killed seconds later. On a devenv that is an ssh session at about 400ms plus whatever the user's rc files do - mine sources twenty files.
- **The keyboard moves into that throwaway.** `tab new` says it does not move the keyboard without `--focus`, and it does not have to: the new tab comes on screen either way, the old one goes hidden, and the keyboard follows the only visible pane. Anyone mid-sentence types into a shell that is about to be closed.
- **Three round trips, not atomic.** A failure between any two leaves a stray tab or a stray pane, and a script has to unwind that itself.

## herdr can already do it in one request

`pane.move`'s destination is a tagged union, and the second variant is exactly this. From the pinned schema, `corpus/herdr-0.8.0/api-schema.json`, `PaneMoveDestination`:

    { "type": "tab",           "tab_id": str, "split": dir, "target_pane_id": str?, "ratio": f32? }
    { "type": "new_tab",       "workspace_id": str?, "label": str? }
    { "type": "new_workspace", "label": str?, "tab_label": str? }

Muster only ever sends the first. `crates/muster-herdr/src/intent.rs:741` says so outright:

> `destination` is a tagged object rather than a bare id: herdr's `pane.move` can also make a tab or a workspace to move into, and the tag is how it tells those apart. Muster only ever names an existing tab, because a drop landed on a row in one.

So this needs no upstream work and no new round trip. It is one destination variant Muster never reaches, and `label` on it means the new tab's name, which the current dance cannot set at all.

## Missing from all three surfaces

- **CLI.** `pane move` requires `--onto <REF>`, and a tab that does not exist yet has no ref.
- **Keymap.** The action list in `docs/configuration.md:63` has `new_tab` and `close_pane` and no way to say "this pane, its own tab".
- **The window.** Dragging a row onto another row moves a pane between tabs. There is no gesture for popping one out.

## Shape

`pane move` is the verb that already owns putting a pane somewhere, so the destination belongs there:

    muster pane move --pane <REF> --new-tab [--name <NAME>]

`--new-tab` excludes `--onto`, the way the position flags on `kan add` exclude each other. `--name` fills herdr's `label`.

The core needs a way to say "a tab of its own" as a move destination. Whether that is a second `BackendIntent` variant beside `MovePane` or a destination enum inside it is the implementer's call - herdr's own shape is a tagged union, but MIP-1 says the core speaks Muster's vocabulary rather than copying herdr's, and "an existing tab" versus "a tab of its own" is Muster vocabulary either way.

A keymap action wants to come with it. Unbound by default, which is what `split_left`, `split_up` and `rename_tab` already do.

The window gesture is a separate question and probably a separate card: dropping a row below the last tab, or onto the gap between two tab groups, both need a drop target that does not exist yet.

## Validating a fix

- One command moves a pane into a tab of its own, and `muster window` shows it alone there.
- No pane is created and destroyed on the way - check the far machine, nothing new started.
- The keyboard does not land anywhere the caller did not ask for.
- `--name` names the new tab.
- Moving the last pane out of a tab still closes the tab it left, as it does today.
- The wire carries one `pane.move` with `type: new_tab`, which the conformance corpus can pin the way `backend-intent.json` already pins the `type: tab` case.
title: ✂️ Moving a pane into a tab of its own takes three commands and a throwaway shell
